$comment: Authored decisions about vocabulary TERMS that no generator can derive and that must
survive regeneration. build_vocab_catalog.py merges this into the emitted codelists.
It exists because _tapp_lib overwrites any codelist whose $id it owns, so an altLabel or a
skos:broader typed into a generated registry/vocab/*.json is destroyed by the next run.
Same pattern as the docs/*.schemapaths.csv sidecars: the generator owns the file, a sidecar
Keyed by the consolidated property's SLUG, then by kind:
slug      notation -> an explicit @id tail, overriding the computed slug
broader   narrower concept slug -> broader concept slug
Every entry is a decision, with the person and date who made it. Nothing is inferred.

sample-preparation-method.$why: Hierarchy authored by Stephen 2026-10-28. Load-bearing, not cosmetic: measured over the 61 per-technique schemes, 'Polished section' appeared in 44 and NEVER co-occurred with any of its three children (11-12 schemes each). The per-technique split encoded different GRANULARITIES of one vocabulary, so before consolidation there was no document in which these relations could be asserted at all. Without them a cross-technique query for polished sections returns the 44 and misses the 11.

target-species-estimation-method.$why: Label variant collapsed per Stephen 2026-10-28 ('use skos:altLabel'), with prefLabel chosen by the shorter-string rule - which also agrees with the corpus, 6 of the 7 files carrying it. The alternate is the sole term of the retired elementEstimationMethod.json, the middle of three generations of this property's name (analyteEstimationMethod -> elementEstimationMethod -> targetSpeciesEstimationMethod), deleted in #242. Kept here deliberately: an obsolete name is exactly what skos:altLabel is for, and it preserves the mapping for any record still carrying the old string. 'By difference' is a genuinely ABSENT term in that outlier, not a variant - do not fold it.

reported-date-type.$why: Ratio slugs authored by Stephen 2026-10-28: '206Pb/238U make 206pb-over-238u'. A blanket '/' -> 'over' rule would be wrong for 14 of the 19 slash notations in the registry, which mean 'or' (MS/MS, MCT/A, W/Mo/Cu, VGI/VOL, Armstrong / Love-Scott). Spacing does not separate the two senses, so the ratios are named explicitly here and everything else keeps a plain hyphen.

limit-of-quantification-method.$why: S/N is signal-to-noise, a ratio. Stephen 2026-10-28.

eels-chemical-state-determination-method.$why: L3/L2 is a white-line intensity ratio, and the notation says so. Stephen 2026-10-28.
